record.original_question: For integers e and m with 3 <= e < m, define the combinatorial upper bound C(e,m) as follows: choose the integer r such that binom(e+r-1, r-1) <= m < binom(e+r, r), set s = m - binom(e+r-1, r-1), and define C(e,m) = binom(e+r-1, r) + s^{<r>} - s, where s^{<r>} is the Macaulay-shift quantity coming from the unique binomial expansion of s used on the page. Determine exactly which pairs (e,m) satisfy R(e,m) = C(e,m), where R(e,m) is the supremum of rho(Gamma) for numerical semigroups Gamma with edim(Gamma) = e + 1 and mult(Gamma) = m.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For a numerical semigroup Γ ⊆ ℕ (a cofinite submonoid of (ℕ,+) containing 0), let mult(Γ) denote the multiplicity of Γ (the smallest positive element of Γ), let edim(Γ) denote the embedding dimension of Γ (the cardinality of its unique minimal system of generators), and let ρ(Γ) denote the reduction number of the maximal ideal of the associated local ring k[[Γ]] (equivalently, the least integer n such that (n+1)·mult(Γ) ∈ Γ + n·mult(Γ) in the standard sense used for one-dimensional local rings, i.e., the index from which the Hilbert function of the associated graded ring stabilizes).

For integers e and m with 3 ≤ e < m, define
   R(e,m) = sup { ρ(Γ) : Γ is a numerical semigroup with edim(Γ) = e+1 and mult(Γ) = m }.

Define the combinatorial quantity C(e,m) as follows. Let r be the unique positive integer such that
   C(e+r−1, r−1) ≤ m < C(e+r, r),
where C(a,b) denotes the binomial coefficient "a choose b". Set
   s = m − C(e+r−1, r−1).
Write s in its r-th Macaulay representation
   s = C(k_r, r) + C(k_{r−1}, r−1) + … + C(k_j, j),
with k_r > k_{r−1} > … > k_j ≥ j ≥ 1, and define
   s^{<r>} = C(k_r+1, r+1) + C(k_{r−1}+1, r) + … + C(k_j+1, j+1).
Finally let
   C(e,m) = C(e+r−1, r) + s^{<r>} − s.

It is known that R(e,m) ≤ C(e,m) for all such e,m. Determine exactly the set of pairs (e,m) with 3 ≤ e < m for which equality R(e,m) = C(e,m) holds.
artifact.status_search_result: The Elias–Robbiano–Valla bound R(e,m) ≤ C(e,m) on reduction numbers / Hilbert function growth (from their 1991 Nagoya Math. J. paper "Number of generators of ideals") is well known to be sharp in many cases but a complete characterization of the equality cases is not recorded as solved in the available literature. Searches did not surface a result giving the exact set of (e,m) for which equality holds, so the problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Number of generators of ideals (Elias–Robbiano–Valla)
status_evidence.snippet: Bounds for v(I) over classes of ideals with preassigned codimension and multiplicity, with sharp bounds attained by suitable ideals.
status_evidence.claim: Original source of the C(e,m) bound; sharpness shown only for some classes, no full characterization given.
